preamble: The loss of [ɛ] is a common process of vowel deletion, both historically (apocope and syncope of unstressed vowels) and synchronically, where a mid front vowel alternates with zero inside a stem. In West Slavic the alternating vowel is the reflex of a former yer, and in Hungarian a closed class of stems drops its last-syllable [ɛ] before vowel-initial suffixes.

examples.note: The unstressed final vowel, levelled to -e (by then [ə]) in Early Middle English, was later lost (apocope).
Vowel-zero alternation: the stem [ɛ] (a reflex of a Proto-Slavic yer) is absent before vowel-initial endings.
Same yer-based alternation as in Polish: [ɛ] in the closed final syllable, zero before a vocalic ending.
One of the roughly 500 'epenthetic' stems: the stem-final syllable's [ɛ] is dropped before a vowel-initial suffix; Takács (2024) analyses the alternation as syncope.

sources: Chociej, J. (2009). Patterns in Polish vowel~zero alternations. Proceedings of the 2009 Annual Conference of the Canadian Linguistic Association. https://cla-acl.artsci.utoronto.ca/pdfs/actes-2009/CLA2009_Chociej.pdf
Takács, D. K. (2024). Constraints on vowel-zero alternations in Hungarian. PhD thesis, MIT. https://dspace.mit.edu/handle/1721.1/157881
Baugh, A. C. & Cable, T. (2013). A History of the English Language (6th ed.). Routledge.
